title: Reduced hammock mapping objects for simplicial pairs
statement: For a small simplicial category $A$ [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], its ordinary degree category $A_n$ has the same objects and mapping sets $A(x,y)_n$, with evaluated identities and composition. A wide simplicial subcategory $U$ is a family of mapping simplicial subsets containing identities and closed under composition in every degree; $U_n$ is the corresponding wide subcategory of $A_n$. For an ordinary category $P$ with a wide subcategory $T$, write $H(P,T)(x,y)_k$ for the set of reduced commutative rectangular zigzags with $k+1$ rows from $x$ to $y$: vertical arrows point down and lie in $T$, endpoint vertical arrows are identities, each horizontal column has uniform direction, leftward arrows lie in $T$, adjacent columns point in opposite directions, and no column is entirely identities; the length-zero diagram is included when $x=y$. Reduction deletes identity columns and composes adjacent columns with the same direction. Define the diagonal reduced hammock enriched category by $\operatorname{diag}H(A,U)(x,y)_n=H(A_n,U_n)(x,y)_n$. Both simplicial operators act together: apply the operator of $A,U$ to every arrow and delete or repeat the corresponding rows, then reduce. The enriched identity is the empty path, and enriched composition concatenates and reduces. For a fixed-object simplicial functor $S:(A,U)\to(B,V)$, its marked mapping map is its restriction (commuting with the mapping-subset inclusions), and the diagonal comparison applies $S_n$ to every grid arrow before reduction.
